Scientists can now read an animal's entire DNA in a day. Understanding it is the hard part.
A genome is billions of letters: A, C, G, T. Genes, the recipes for proteins, hide inside, and finding them takes experts.
Hugging Face just released Carbon-A, an AI that reads raw DNA and marks the genes itself.
It has 1.2 billion parameters, and it reads about ninety-eight thousand letters at once.
One model covers mammals, birds, plants and fungi. No separate expert for each species.
It even handled a pond microbe that rewrites the code: two stop signals mean glutamine instead.
Run across forty-eight thousand genome assemblies, it flagged 566 million possible genes.
Lab tests in cats, chickens and Arabidopsis backed several genes the reference list was missing.
They're candidates, not proven proteins yet. But life's map just got more readable. Follow LATOON.
